$comment: Contrast style: for readers with low vision or colour-vision differences, and for any report that must meet WCAG AAA. Text 7:1, marks 4.5:1 in both modes (meta.level AAA), Atkinson Hyperlegible, 2 px borders, direction glyphs on every variance so colour is never the only cue.

meta.label: Contrast
meta.summary: Maximum legibility: black on white (or white on black), AAA contrast, a typeface designed for low vision, strong borders, and every variance carrying a direction glyph as well as its colour.

relaxes.what: 2 px borders around tiles and cards.
relaxes.why: Clear boundaries for low vision and for screen magnifiers, where only part of the page is visible.

relaxes.what: Atkinson Hyperlegible, a typeface designed for low-vision readers, at larger sizes.
relaxes.why: Distinct letterforms (1/l/I, 0/O, 5/S) and generous spacing improve legibility.

relaxes.what: Larger text: body 17 px, labels 15 px, figures 36 px.
relaxes.why: Readable without zooming; still fits 390 px.

relaxes.what: Every variance label carries a direction glyph (▲ ▼) next to its colour.
relaxes.why: Colour is never the only cue (WCAG 1.4.1); the glyph follows the sign, the colour the impact.
relaxes.condition: The glyph follows the sign, never the tone; a variance shown as zero has no glyph and no colour.

relaxes.what: A dark theme of white on pure black when the reader picks dark.
relaxes.why: Many low-vision readers need inverted contrast; the notation and the impact hue families are kept at AAA contrast.
